question.content:
The nation of Eoth can produce two goods: good L and good M. The production possibilities curve for Eoth is below.

[[☃ image 1]]

**What does the shape of the PPC say about the production of these two goods?**

[[☃ radio 1]]

options.alt: A coordinate plane with grid lines at each unit plots one concave curve. The horizontal axis is labeled Good M and ranges from 0 to 10 in increments of 1. The vertical axis is labeled Good L and ranges from 0 to 10 in increments of 1. A production possibilities curve runs from (0, 8) to (9, 0), curving outward.
options.caption: Production possibilities for Eoth

choices.clue: The bowed shape of the PPC here signifies that there are increasing opportunity costs which occurs when there are different uses of resources to produce two different goods.
choices.content: Goods L and M require very different resources to produce.

choices.clue: If the goods require similar resources to produce the PPC would be a nearly straight line from a point on the vertical axis to a point on the horizontal axis.
choices.content: Goods L and M require similar resources to produce.

choices.clue: If this were the case, the PPC would be a completely straight line from a point on the vertical axis to a point on the horizontal axis.
choices.content: Goods L and M require identical resources to produce.

choices.clue: If more of M could be produced without giving up any of L, the PPC would be a horizontal line.
choices.content: There is zero opportunity cost in terms of Good L given up as output of Good M increases.

choices.clue: If this were the case the PPC would be bowed inward towards the origin.
choices.content: The opportunity cost of Good M decreases in terms of the amount of L given up as output of M increases.
